newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Dec jobs and 1996 GDP.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Dec jobs and 1996 GDP.

text.p: The following are views expressed by economists after German December unemployment rose 48,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.156 million and provisional 1996 GDP rose a real 1.4 percent against 1.9 percent in 1995.
ULF RASSAT, ECONOMIST AT BAYERISCHE HYPOTHEKEN UND WECHSELBANK IN MUNICH:

"The GDP numbers are a bit weaker than we expected and that means the fourth quarter must have been weak. Unemployment is slightly above what we expected and that seems to be caused by the construction sector above all. You can see that in the figures for eastern Germany."
GERTRUD TRAUD, ECONOMIST, BANK JULIUS BAER, FRANKFURT:
"The unemployment figures were a little bit disappointing. We think the negative trend will continue and unemployment will continue to rise until February when it could reach a peak of 11.3 percent.

"Meanwhile, we had expected GDP to grow 1.3 percent, so 1.4 percent was a bit higher than expected, but that was probably due to strong exports. The figures for the East were disappointing. We had expected 2.4 percent, rather than two percent."

"The GDP figure conformed with market expectations. As long as there is no revision to the figures, that means a growth rate of 0.4 to 0.5 percent in GDP for the last quarter of 1996. For this year we expect growth of an average of 2.7 percent.

"In the jobs market, weather played the biggest part and the seasonal effect was once more negative. That means that demand did not keep pace with production in Germany. I think the pressure will rise on the central bank to reduce interest rates. The Bundesbank cannot just stand by and do nothing when unemployment reaches 4.5 million in two months."
